title: Smart Serving Savings — Adaptive Compression & Cache Coordination
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: Deliver a coordinated initiative that combines lightweight adaptive compression (model quantization profiles and token-aware compression heuristics) with an intelligent cache coordination layer and workload-aware batching to reduce per-token serving costs by 15–25% for core workloads without degrading tail latency or generation quality.

Why now: unit cost pressure is a top three commercial blocker for mid-market customers migrating from MVP to paid usage. Prior efforts (single-strategy quantization pilots, generic batching improvements) showed isolated wins but did not compound across the stack. This initiative focuses on cross-layer coordination: (1) compression/quantization profiles that trade bits for fidelity selectively, (2) prefix/KV cache orchestration that maximizes hit rate across common prompt patterns, and (3) dynamic batching policies tied to SLO classes and cost targets.

Success metrics (OKRs):
- Reduce host API gross cost-per-1M tokens for sampled PLG accounts by 20% (OKR-KR1).
- Increase KV/prefix cache effective hit rate to >= 35% on nightly production traffic (OKR-KR2).
- Keep 99th-percentile token-generation latency regression < 10% for priority models (OKR-KR3).
- Maintain automated quality checks (eval set pass rate) >= 98% vs baseline for targeted prompts (OKR-KR4).

Scope (what we will do):
- Implement 2 adaptive quantization profiles per priority model (aggressive + conservative) with automated selection logic based on prompt fingerprinting and customer SLO tier.
- Build a Cache Coordination service that tracks per-route prefix popularity, TTL heuristics, and backoff for cache stampedes; expose configurable policies via Console.
- Extend scheduler to support workload-aware batching: per-route batch windows, latency budget signals, and cost-target-driven batching thresholds.
- Add evaluation harness and synthetic replay runs to measure quality regressions across 40 curated prompts and 8 internal production routes.

Out-of-scope (for this cycle):
- Full model architecture changes or custom kernel work (will be tracked in ENG backlog).
- Major console redesign (we will add small UI for toggles/metrics only).

Risks and mitigations:
- Quality regressions from aggressive quantization: mitigate with staged rollout (canary -> A/B -> full), automatic rollback on eval regressions, and manual override per-customer.
- Cache eviction thrashing with multi-tenant popularity shifts: mitigate with adaptive TTLs and cross-tenant isolation knobs for Dedicated customers.
- Scheduler complexity causing latency spikes: start with conservative batching windows and enable gradual increases via feature flags.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1–3: Engineering spike + quantization profile training and correctness tests; define fingerprinting heuristics.
- Week 4–6: Implement Cache Coordination service + internal replay for hit-rate estimation.
- Week 7–9: Integrate batching scheduler changes; run canaries on low-risk routes; monitor metrics.
- Week 10–12: Broaden A/B to PLG cohort, collect econ and quality metrics, document runbook and Console controls.

Acceptance criteria:
- Automated tests and evaluation harness show <=2% loss in quality for conservative quant profile and <=5% for aggressive on the 40-prompt set.
- Production canary demonstrates >=10% cost reduction on selected routes and cache hit-rate >=25% before global rollout.
- Console surfaces per-route cost delta, cache hit-rate, and quantization profile used; PM sign-off obtained.

Notes on trade-offs:
- We prioritize user-visible cost wins with bounded quality impact over maximal theoretical savings that require heavy manual tuning.
- Conservative quant profile should be the default for Enterprise and Dedicated customers; enable aggressive options for PLG/self-serve with explicit warnings.
